A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Circuit Transformer by the same authors, despite the changed subtitle and substantial revision. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and v2's Appendix A.1–A.9 are readable. v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original truth-table prediction experiments with tiny Transformers and circuit synthesis experiments on 960 random circuits (Section 4, Tables 1–2).

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on random circuits and IWLS circuit windows, including neural comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and failure examples (Section 5, Appendix A.8–A.9).

M1.justification: The core depth-first encoding, tree positional encoding, Transformer architecture, equivalence masking, and size-based reward are retained. v2 refines components through functional rather than solely structural node merging, greedy rather than sampled token selection, cached masking checks, and revised MCTS search organization (Sections 4.3–4.5, Appendices A.3 and A.5). The wildcard terminology largely reformulates v1's partially constructed circuits.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on real circuit substructures extracted from IWLS 2023, extending beyond v1's synthetic circuits. It retains random 8-input, 2-output circuit optimization but removes the separate 4-input, 1-output truth-table prediction task and its tiny-model experiments.

E2.justification: v1's synthesis comparison uses Resyn2 alongside Circuit Transformer and its MCTS variants. v2 adds actually trained Boolean Chain and AIGER Transformer baselines, each evaluated with and without beam search, while retaining Resyn2 (Table 2). These substantially expand the comparator set; they are not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: The synthetic dataset changes from 20 million circuits to 15 million with an 89/1/10 training/validation/test split; random test cases increase from 960 to 10,240. Batch size changes from 96 to 128, training from one million batches to five epochs, and generation limits from 100 to 200 tokens. v2 also changes reported uniqueness requirements, search budgets, and failure scoring: unsuccessful outputs receive their original circuit size instead of being excluded from the Circuit Transformer mean.

E4.justification: v2 adds ablations removing tree positional encoding and equivalence masking, runtime/overhead analysis, and concrete failure cases distinguishing inequivalence, malformed representations, and length exhaustion (Tables 3–6). v1's tiny-model layer-count study is removed, while its MCTS step/rollout sweep is replaced by total-playout comparisons. These substantially change the questions investigated beyond aggregate benchmark performance.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports standard deviations of circuit sizes in Tables 3–4 and dispersion of input circuit sizes in Section 5. These describe variation across circuits, not uncertainty across training runs. Neither version reports repeated-training counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The synthesis results are replaced under revised conditions, and IWLS, baseline, ablation, timing, and failure results are added. For example, v1 Table 2 reports 9.127 gates for MCTS-CT at S=10, R=20 versus Resyn2's 9.578; v2 Table 2 reports 13.73 for K=100 versus 14.56 on its new random test set. These are not same-setting gains or losses. v1's truth-table accuracy results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 develops explicit equivalence classes, three-valued logic, the SIMEQ relation, and cutoff properties, substantially extending v1's informal partial-truth-table argument. Appendix A.2 supplies proofs of inheritability, incrementality, backtrack elimination, and representational completeness; A.3 develops the O(N·2^N·d) masking computation. These are substantive mathematical additions despite retention of the core generation idea.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes generative circuit design analogous to language modeling and MCTS outperforming Resyn2. v2 retains equivalence preservation but adds explicit claims of formally justified, backtracking-free constrained generation and superiority over neural alternatives on synthetic and real circuit benchmarks. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion substantially redefine the contribution around precise constrained generation.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations and applicability limits: it discusses the small action space, sequence growth from unfolding high-fanout graphs, and masking computation's dependence on input count. Appendix A.8 distinguishes direct masking overhead from additional decoding time caused by longer valid sequences. Failure interpretation also becomes more detailed, separating equivalence preservation from successful completion within the length limit.

D1.justification: v2 adds the implementation framework, positional-encoding depth, dataset-generation pseudocode, canonicalization information, IWLS processing instructions, hardware specifications, and 75-hour training time (Section 5, Appendices A.6–A.7). These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's architecture and basic training settings. However, v1's explicit learning rate of 10^-3 is no longer supplied.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning through backtracking, action masking for routing, SAT acceleration, circuit complexity, circuit representations, and generative logic research such as Boolformer. Several earlier LLM-focused references disappear. The discussion shifts from a brief ML-for-EDA overview toward distinguishing exact constrained generation from probabilistic approaches and simpler feasibility masks.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, methods narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces a separate problem description and presents general constrained generation before circuit encoding. Detailed positional-encoding explanation moves to Appendix A.4, and algorithms and supporting material are redistributed across the main text and appendix.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes a single-column conference layout, with substantial visual redesign. v2 replaces the original pipeline illustration with separate training/inference diagrams, adds Boolean-function, backtracking, DAG/tree, and caching illustrations, and removes the hypothetical truth-table Transformer diagram. Result tables are reorganized around two benchmarks, with additional detailed and failure-example tables.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's largely informal justification and synthetic-only validation, v2 adds explicit mathematical support, controlled neural comparisons, real circuit windows, and ablations testing the central components. These substantially strengthen the evidence for equivalence-preserving generation and clarify its computational and completion limits. The omitted learning rate and small reporting inconsistencies, such as IWLS Resyn2 size being 16.82 in Table 2 but 16.83 in Table 4, modestly offset these gains without outweighing them.
